subject: AtlasCloud: PO requirements & vendor-setup kickoff
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@atlascloud.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AtlasCloud: PO requirements & vendor-setup kickoff

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for the pilot. I wanted to kick off vendor onboarding so procurement has everything they need to issue PO and set up billing. Quick checklist of what Procurement requires from AtlasCloud to generate a PO and complete vendor setup: 

- Vendor legal name and remit-to address
- Completed vendor-setup form (I attached a PDF)
- W-9 (for US entities) or equivalent tax form
- Purchase order contact and billing email
- Any required PO line-item breakdown (unit descriptions, qty, unit cost, term)
- If you need a vendor-specific statement of work (SOW), please attach

Can you confirm which items you can provide this week and whether AtlasCloud needs any specific PO language (e.g., customer-specific invoice instructions, tax exemptions)? Our target timeline: vendor setup + PO issuance by EOD Thu 30 Jul so we can start provisioning Dedicated capacity next week. If anything needs legal review we can pause the PO until redlines are resolved, but flag it early.

Attachments: vendor-setup-form.pdf (fillable)

Next steps:
- Lisa: confirm which items you’ll send and expected dates
- Mina: will route to Procurement (Vivek) as soon as we receive completed forms
- Dev: please stand by for any technical questions about line-item breakdown or SKU mapping.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Sr. Manager, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0189

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@atlascloud.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlascloud.io
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasCloud: PO requirements & vendor-setup kickoff

Mina —

Thanks, and great to get this moving. Quick answers: 

- We can return the vendor-setup form and W-9 by end of day tomorrow (28 Jul).
- Billing contact: finance@atlascloud.io (Mary Torres)
- Preferred remit-to: Atlas Cloud, Inc., 1200 Market St, Suite 500, San Francisco, CA 94103
- PO language: please include standard PO referencing our internal PO number field and "Net 30" payment terms — we don’t require any special clauses.
- Line-item detail: we prefer a single line for "Redwood Dedicated - Pilot (1 x GPU pool)" with unit cost and term (monthly) and a second line for one-time setup fee. Dev is copied for any SKU clarification.

Attaching a signed W9 and our procurement intake checklist. If you need the SOW signed first we can loop legal, but for procurement we just need vendor setup and PO.

Attachments: signed-W9-AtlasCloud.pdf; atlas-procurement-checklist.xlsx

Best,
Lisa
Director, Procurement
AtlasCloud

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@atlascloud.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasCloud: PO requirements & vendor-setup kickoff

Lisa —

Perfect, and thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifications for Procurement to avoid PO revisions: 

1) Line-item naming convention: please confirm the exact wording you want on the invoice. Our preferred default (if you don’t specify) is: "Redwood Dedicated — Reserved GPU Pool (pilot)" for the recurring line and "Redwood Onboarding Setup Fee" for the one-time.

2) Unit of measure: we bill monthly for reserved capacity. For the pilot PO, we’ll include unit = "month", qty = 1, and a line for prorated partial month if start date is mid-cycle.

3) Billing contact/email: we’ll set Mary Torres (finance@atlascloud.io) as the invoice recipient. Any PO approval routing on your side we should be aware of? If your AP team requires a PO number before payment, we’ll add their PO reference to the invoice header.

4) Redlines: I attached a short redline-summary.xlsx with the few minor contract items we're expecting — none typically block PO issuance, but flagging in case Legal needs to see them.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
- 28 Jul (EOD): AtlasCloud returns completed form + W-9 (Lisa) — received per your note
- 29 Jul (morning): Redwood Procurement (Vivek) creates vendor record and issues draft PO to AtlasCloud for internal approval
- 29 Jul (end): AtlasCloud confirms PO or requests edits; if edits, allow 1 business day for redraft
- 30 Jul: Target PO issuance (final signed PO) and vendor setup complete

Vivek — can you confirm you’ll pick this up as soon as Lisa’s paperwork lands? If you want me to route the final PO to legal or finance for sign-off, say the word.

Thanks again —
Mina

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@atlascloud.io>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasCloud: PO requirements & vendor-setup kickoff

Thanks team —

I got the W-9 and checklist from Lisa earlier. I will: 
- Create the vendor record in our AP system today
- Draft the PO using the naming convention Mina suggested (I’ll include AtlasCloud’s PO reference field)
- Send over a draft PO to Lisa for internal approval by 29 Jul 10:00 AM PT

Dev — I may need a quick line-item confirmation from you: can you confirm the one-time setup fee amount to include (we typically use the number in redline-summary.xlsx) and whether we should add an explicit "prorated partial month" line or include it in notes? If you can reply by 29 Jul 8:30 AM, I’ll keep to the timeline.

Attachments referenced: redline-summary.xlsx (internal), draft-po-template.xml (internal stub)

-Vivek
Head of Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference
